plan.code_changes: Added _round_pipe, an otherwise identical copy of _round_stream whose full-tile loop uses tl.range(..., num_stages=2) so the next GM->UB load overlaps the current tile's convert+2-add+store. _build selects _round_pipe for float16/bfloat16 and keeps the single-stage _round_stream for float32 (a 2-stage fp32 path would need about 192KB UB). expected_effect.mechanism: Overlapping the 16KB next-tile DMA with vector work raises effective GM->UB rate toward the reference's ~43GB/s per core; timing-7 bf16 4096x4096 should fall from 23.5us toward ~20.5us and timing-3 fp16 from 21.2us toward ~19us.

plan.strategy: Raise the streaming tile to 16384 elements on the 16-bit path only, which the device-level probe showed to be ~5% faster than 8192 at grid=40.
plan.code_changes: In _geometry, the streaming tile cap is now dtype dependent: 16-bit (float16/bfloat16) inputs use BLOCK=16384, float32 keeps BLOCK=8192 (a 16384 fp32 tile would need ~192KB UB). plan.hypothesis: The residual 16-bit streaming gap is per-tile transfer/handshake overhead rather than pipeline depth; a 32KB tile should lift timing-7 from 23.5us toward 22.3us and timing-3 from 21.2us toward 20.3us.

expected_effect.mechanism: Doubling the 16-bit tile to 32KB per GM<->UB burst and per program iteration reduces per-tile instruction and handshake overhead; device-side probe measured bf16 4096x4096 at 23.09us with BLOCK=16384 versus 24.32us with BLOCK=8192 (same protocol, host floor 11.35us).

conclusion.perf_gap_analysis: Both targeted predictions held at the workload level: timing-7 bf16 4096x4096 fell from 23.492us to 22.494us (speedup 0.8113 -> 0.8549) and timing-3 fp16 from 21.240us to 20.334us (1.4794 -> 1.5512); timing-6 bf16 1M also improved 14.624 -> 13.372us. conclusion.root_cause: Two regimes. (b) N<=1048576 cases (9 workloads): 16.5-19.4 us against a 12.4-14.5 us reference, flat across a 1024x range in N, so the 2.6-4.7 us gap is a constant host-dispatch/launch cost, not workload work. Profiler (msprof) produced zero artifacts on 5 attempts (base collection never signaled completion), so no counter-level pipeline split is available; the dtype-flatness argument above is eval-latency evidence only.
conclusion.perf_gap_analysis: geo_mean 0.4911 with all 30/30 workloads passing and matched_ratio 1.0. The three large workloads carry the whole deficit: t3 0.1169, t7 0.0705, t11 0.3552 versus 0.643-0.846 for the nine small ones. Reference latency itself scales with bytes on the large cases (0.0314 fp16 / 0.0191 bf16 / 0.0988 fp32), i.e. the reference sits near cache-bandwidth rates, while the candidate is pinned at ~0.27 ms regardless of dtype: eliminating the arithmetic redundancy is the only lever with enough range to move the geometric mean, and the small-case ceiling (<=4.7 us of host overhead) is worth at most a few percent.
conclusion.next_suggestion: Replace the floor/fraction/int32-parity/3x-select RNE core of _round_value with the magic-constant form: r = (|v| + 2^23) - 2^23 (the add is exact RNE at ulp=1 for all |v| < 2^23, and the existing passthrough select at |v| >= 2^23 covers the already-integral range), drop the redundant NaN/Inf guard because NaN falls through the compare and Inf takes the passthrough branch, and keep abs() plus the sign-bit re-application (the magic path yields +0.0 for small negative inputs while round(-0.4) must be -0.0). Keep the DECIMALS!=0 scale/div_rn tail. This cuts ~24 ops/element to ~9 and removes several live FP32 temporaries; if the large cases do not drop by at least ~40%, the ALU-op hypothesis is falsified and the next attack must be block/UB geometry or a single-instruction RNE intrinsic (tl.math.rint / round-to-nearest-even convert) instead.
conclusion.debug_lesson: For this operator the dtype-flatness of the candidate latency across fp16/bf16/fp32 is by itself a discriminating signal: an MTE-bound kernel cannot be flat against a byte-scaling reference. msprof collection currently fails at the base stage on this server, so plan to discriminate hypotheses with eval-latency structure plus bounded debug microbenchmarks rather than pipeline counters.

conclusion.strategy_evolution: Tile tuning is now understood: BLOCK=16384 for 16-bit is the best streaming tile, grid=40 is optimal, and the remaining work is host-path slimming plus combining both verified wins in one candidate.
